text: Our looks all that matter. And what do I think about the Black Pill? I initially prepared this video exclusively for my paid subscriber, but once I finished the script, I felt that the message was simply too important not to share it with everyone. So please, like, comment, and share this video so that it reaches more people, especially young men who may need to hear this message. And of course, if you would like to support my work directly, consider becoming a paid subscriber. Exclusive videos, priority DMs, and access to the special members chat are waiting for you. Let me start with this. I do not like Black Pill ideology, at least in the way I understand it. I think it can be very detrimental to men, and it goes directly against what I preach on this channel. So what is the Black Pill? In simple terms, the way I understand it, it's a very fatalistic view of dating. It says that some men are born as winners and others as losers, and that your success in dating is largely determined by things you cannot change. Facial features, height, race, bone structure, and genetics. According to them, there is a strict ceiling, and even if you improve your appearance or other aspects of your life, it will still not make much difference, because you were not born attractive enough. Now, is there some truth in the idea that life is unfair? Of course. For an average guy, there are certain things that are either impossible or extremely difficult to change. Your height, race, or basic bone structure. Some men are simply born with more advantages than others. But so what? Does that mean you should stop trying to become the best version of yourself and do absolutely nothing? Take money as an example. Some people are born into rich families, while others are born into poor ones. Does that mean that if you were born poor, you should not even try, because you can never earn decent money? Of course not. That would be nonsense. Even though there are things an average man cannot change, there are still plenty of things he can improve. Work on your style. Find a haircut that suits you. Take care of your hygiene and grooming. Develop your social skills. Find great hobbies and build an interesting lifestyle. Work on your career and earn more money. And most importantly, actually do something about dating. That is one of my biggest problems with the black belt. It doesn't simply acknowledge that some men have disadvantages. It takes those disadvantages and turns them into a reason to surrender. It kills motivation and takes away hope. Yes, the path may not be easy. I think I have told you before that it probably took me more than a decade to become noticeably better at dating. But you should never give up. Now, regarding how important looks are. Looks are very important. Overall, the first impression depends a lot on how you look. And in my personal experience, the more Western the dating culture is, the more heavily looks are emphasized. Social media and dating apps make appearance even more important. This is exactly why I put so much emphasis on working on yourself. Exercising, dressing well, taking care of your hygiene and grooming, and presenting yourself properly. But are looks everything? No, they are not. I know very good-looking guys who struggle with women because they are passive, socially awkward, afraid to make a move, or simply underdeveloped in other areas of their lives. And I know relatively average-looking guys who have much richer and more interesting dating lives than many handsome men, simply because they are more well-rounded, socially skilled, interesting, and proactive. Looks affect your starting position. They may influence how many opportunities you receive and how easy the first step is. But they do not completely determine what you do with those opportunities, or whether you create opportunities for yourself. So my message is not that looks do not matter. That would be dishonest. My message is this. Accept the reality of your situation, work with what you have, and keep improving.
